steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere and shorter wavelengths of light (blue) are scattered much more effectively than longer wavelengths (red). As sunlight enters the atmosphere, blue light is scattered in all directions across the sky, making the entire sky appear to glow blue when viewed from the ground. At sunset, light travels through more atmosphere to reach your eyes, scattering away most of the blue light and leaving the longer red and orange wavelengths, which is why sunsets appear warm-toned.
